24.0.0.en: Aaron had four sons, two of whom died because they offered strange fire (Num 3:4), and two remained, Eleazar and Ithamar.

24.1.0.en: David met with Zadok the high priest, who was of the descendants of Eleazar, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar the other high priest, that is, the king met with the chiefs of the priests to divide the priests into divisions. Here we see the importance of organization in service and of defining responsibility, so that the work may be accomplished with success, order and arrangement.

24.1.1.en: Note: Abiathar the high priest was the father of Ahimelech, and his father was also called Ahimelech (1 Sam 23:6).

24.1.2.en: May you divide your responsibilities, to carry out each one at its proper time every day, or every week, or more, so that your responsibilities are accomplished with success and precision, and so that you do not forget any responsibility, and God will rejoice in your organization and your care.

24.2.0.en: Eleazar had 16 chiefs among his descendants, while Abiathar had fewer descendants, eight chiefs, and so the divisions of the priests were divided into 24 divisions. We notice that the Book of Revelation speaks to us of 24 priests (Rev 4:4), like the number of the twenty-four divisions of the priests mentioned here. The fewer descendants of Abiathar the high priest were due to God's curse on the house of Eli and his descendants, so their number became small (1 Sam 2:30, 31).

24.3.0.en: Lots were cast among the twenty-four chiefs to arrange them in the service of the sanctuary and the house of God. Perhaps the sanctuary means the ark of the covenant that was in Jerusalem, while the house of God is the tabernacle that was in Gibeon. After the building of the Temple, these divisions worked in its service and in all that it contained. Perhaps the division and the election by lot was to know who would begin the service, and then who would follow, since each division served for a week and then rested, and in the second half of the year served another week in order, with all the divisions meeting together at the great feasts.

24.3.1.en: The lot is a system that guarantees justice, with no partiality toward anyone (Prov 16:33), so that each one is assured his opportunity before God, as happened with the Apostles when they chose a replacement for Judas Iscariot (Acts 1:26).

24.4.0.en: The lots were cast, and perhaps this was by writing the names of the sons of Eleazar, each on a piece of pottery, and putting them in one jar, and the sons of Ithamar in another jar, and then they would take one from this jar and one from the other jar, while Shemaiah the scribe, one of the Levites, wrote the names of the divisions in order as it appeared from the lot. So after he wrote eight of the descendants of Eleazar and the eight who were of the descendants of Ithamar, he wrote the remaining eight of the descendants of Eleazar. All of this was by lot.

24.5.0.en: He mentions the names that came out by lot, that is, the order of the twenty-four divisions, so that they might begin their priestly service.

24.5.1.en: Our teacher St. Luke the Evangelist tells us that Zacharias the priest, the father of John the Baptist, was of the division of Abijah, that is, the eighth division (Lk 1:5). The twenty-four divisions of the priests continued as a system in force until the days of Christ, as shown by the mention that Zacharias was of the division of Abijah, and that his turn of service came, so he entered the Temple and saw the angel in the sanctuary.

25.0.s.en: (1) The sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun

25.0.0.en: The captains of the host: what is meant is the host of God that serves Him, that is, the chief priests, and perhaps they are the chiefs of the twenty-four priestly divisions (ch. 24:7-19). Three men were distinguished in praise and singing, for their voices and their ability to play musical instruments, namely Asaph of the clan of the Gershonites, Heman of the clan of the Kohathites, and Jeduthun, who is also called Ethan (ch. 6:44), of the sons of Merari; that is, the chiefs of the singers were from all the clans of the Levites. David set them apart for the service of praise and prophesying, that is, chanting the psalms that are full of prophecies, for praise may be called prophesying, as it was in the days of Samuel (1 Sam 10:5). The musical instruments used were psalteries, harps and cymbals.

25.0.1.en: The service of praise and singing before the house of the Lord was a great work, because it is a spiritual work, full of feeling and of the repetition of the word of God, which satisfies the soul.

25.0.2.en: The sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun were organized into divisions to carry out the service of praise before the house of God continually.

25.1.0.en: Here he mentions the sons of Asaph, who are four, and the sons of Jeduthun, who are six, although the sixth, who is Shimei, is not mentioned here but is mentioned in (v. 17). And the sons of Heman are fourteen. All these praised and gave thanks to God by the side of the king, that is, before the house of the Lord.

25.1.1.en: He singles out Heman as "the seer," and what is meant is that he sees the word of God that is in the psalms and declares it before the king, and perhaps he had a standing and spirituality that made the Bible give him the title of seer. Heman's praise was great in the eyes of God, so his singing was described as "to lift up the horn," and the horn is the horn of an animal, which is a symbol of strength, and the horn was also used as a musical instrument like the trumpet. Among God's blessings on Heman was that He gave him 14 sons and three daughters whom he taught the praise of God, and they excelled in it and led others in praise.

25.1.2.en: Here we see the fathers' concern to teach praise, so they loved it and it became their service, in which they were distinguished before God.

25.1.3.en: Be concerned to teach your children how to love God, especially through the ways that you love, such as the Liturgies, or the Midnight Praise (Tasbeha), or the Agpeya, or the Bible ... for what you love you will speak of from your heart and it will reach the hearts of your children, whether in the home, or in the Church, or among all whom you love and who love you, and so you will rejoice the heart of God, and your spiritual depth will increase, and you will be established in the service of God.

25.2.0.en: The number of singers from the descendants of Asaph, Jeduthun and Heman was 288 men. The service of praise was under the leadership of the three chiefs mentioned, and these singers acquired an experience in praise that drew the hearts of the worshipers who came to the house of God.

28.0.0.en: The writer of this book pointed out in (ch. 23:1) that David had grown old and made his son Solomon king, and after this in (chs. 23 - 27) he mentioned the arrangements that David had prepared for the building of the Temple and the order of service in it. David had grown very old, as is mentioned in (1 Kgs 1:1, 2), so that he could not bear the cold of the air, and they covered him with clothes and he needed a nurse. But he strengthened himself to bid farewell to his people and charge them how to walk with God, and to declare Solomon king after him. So he gathered all his princes, that is, all those in authority in his kingdom, among them the captains of the divisions that served him, a division each month, mentioned in (ch. 24), and he mentions among them the eunuchs. This is the first time we find mention of this class with the kings of the people of God, although it existed with the kings of the nations. This means either that the people of God imitated the nations and castrated some people to serve the women, or that it was a rank in which this name, eunuchs, was used, but they were ordinary people.

28.1.0.en: David was eager and strengthened himself, so he rose from his bed and stood on his feet, that is, he did not sit on a throne and speak as kings customarily do, and this shows:

28.1.1.en: 1- David's humility and his love for his people, which he confirms by his saying "my brethren, and my people."

28.1.2.en: 2- David's concern to charge his people to submit to God.

28.1.3.en: 3- His concern to declare Solomon's kingship.

28.1.4.en: 4- His longing to build a house in which the ark of the covenant of God would rest (a resting place), to be a footstool for the feet of God, since His throne is in heaven, because the ark used to be moved about before this, when it was in the tabernacle of meeting.

28.1.5.en: 5- David's sense that this was the last word he would address to his people made him revive.

28.2.0.en: In humility David declares his unworthiness to build the house of the Lord, as God declared to him, because he was occupied throughout his life with many wars.

28.3.0.en: David's submission is shown in his thanking God for choosing him as king, because God chose the tribe of Judah and from it the house of Jesse, from which God chose David. Although Judah was not the firstborn of Jacob, nor was David the firstborn of Jesse, it was the grace of God that gave him to become king. So he declares his unworthiness of the kingship and affirms that God is the One who chose him, and then afterward chose his son Solomon by name to reign after him, so that no one would object to him.

28.4.0.en: David declared clearly that God had chosen Solomon and also charged him with building His house, and he declared God's fatherhood and care for Solomon, and His readiness to establish his kingdom forever, on condition that Solomon submit to the commandments of God. This was a type of what actually happened, for Christ came from the descendants of David and Solomon to reign forever.

28.5.0.en: David concludes his word to the leaders of his people with the necessity of keeping the commandments of God and submitting to Him, so that the land of Canaan may remain an inheritance for them, and it is a symbol of the new earth, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven. This address, David declares, is in the sight of the Lord and in the audience of His congregation, that is, God is present and a witness to David's words, so that He may make His people submit and hold fast to the commandments of God.

28.5.1.en: Your way to happiness and to receiving all of God's blessings is to hold fast to His commandments, so read the word of God every day and examine yourself by it, if you have strayed from it, and God will establish you in His house and give you a place in His Kingdom.

28.6.s.en: (2) David's charge to Solomon and his handing over to him the plan for building the house

28.6.0.en: After David charged his leaders, he gave a special charge to his son Solomon, because he would be the leader of the kingdom after him, and he commanded him as follows:

28.6.1.en: 1- To know God, that is, to recall His works with the fathers and to know His commandments, and David here affirms to Solomon that He is "the God of thy father," because Solomon loves David, and this increases his holding fast to God.

28.6.2.en: 2- To worship God with all that the Law and its rites prescribe, and that this be with all his heart and with longing and desire, that is, he should seek the worship of God in order to perform it enjoying it.

28.6.3.en: 3- To remember that God knows hidden things, so that he is with Him with all his heart, and worship is not a mere outward performance, and he does not sin, because God sees him, even in his private room, away from eyes.

28.6.4.en: 4- David encourages Solomon that if he holds fast to the commandments of God and His worship, he will feel God's presence with him and His blessing keeping and covering him, and he warns him that if he is negligent and leaves the commandments of God, God will forsake him and reject him because of his persistence in sin, and nothing awaits him but eternal torment.

28.6.5.en: 5- He reminded him of the grace of God in choosing him to build the house of the Lord, and commanded him to be strong and work with all his heart.

28.6.6.en: Be concerned to charge your children and those around you and teach them the commandments of God, and even if they reject your words, they may act on them after a while. Do not be lazy because of your preoccupations, or because those around you do not listen, and your prayer for them will support them and encourage them to live with God.

28.7.0.en: Porch: the court. The upper chambers thereof: upper rooms. The inner chambers thereof: its rooms. The house of the mercy seat: the Holy of Holies, where the ark is covered by the cherubim.

28.7.1.en: Snuffers: those for the lampstands, to trim their lamps and light them.

28.7.2.en: Basons: for sprinkling water or blood. Cups: goblets. God declared to David the details of the building of the Temple precisely and in writing, and it may have been by means of an angel. All this David handed over to Solomon, so that he would do everything in the house of the Lord according to the pattern that God had made known to David, for the house of God is too great to be arranged by a man, but God Himself arranges His house and man carries out what God declares, as He declared of old to Moses the details of the tabernacle of meeting (Ex 25:8, 9).

28.8.0.en: In the end David encouraged Solomon to do all that God had charged, and David's strong relationship with God appears in his saying "God, even my God," to call his son to this intimate relationship. He promised him that God would be with him until he completed the building of His house, and encouraged him not to fear any obstacles, or problems, or enemies that might appear before him, especially since Solomon had not yet completed twenty years of age at that time. God fulfilled His promise, so Solomon was strengthened and was not troubled by those who rebelled against him, and he completed the house of the Lord with all diligence.

28.9.0.en: Skilful with wisdom: one who has a craft, an artist and gifted in it.

28.9.1.en: David reminded Solomon that he had arranged for him the divisions of the priests and the Levites and the chiefs and the artists who were able to do the work of the house of the Lord and everything in it, and all the people, all of whom would help him to complete this great work. Donations for the Temple, and David's prayer and death

29.0.0.en: David continued his words with the leaders of his people, whom he had gathered in (ch. 28:1), and showed them that because of the young age of Solomon, whom God alone chose from among all his brothers to be king after him over His people, and likewise God's command that Solomon would be the one to build the Temple of God, and that the Temple is for God and not for man, that is, it is very great and no man is able to build it except with God's help, he had therefore prepared all that he could prepare for this Temple, as will appear in (v. 2).

29.1.0.en: Onyx stones: a precious stone in which colors appear in parallel lines.

29.1.2.en: Kohl-black stones: very black, or white with parts that are very black.

29.1.4.en: Here David mentioned the kinds of materials that he had prepared for the building of the Temple of the Lord, which contain everything that is precious, whether gold, or silver, or precious stones, and this shows how great was David's love and magnification of God, and that he prepared with all his energy all that he was able, for he says "with all my might," and whoever gives to God with all his energy receives a blessing beyond what he imagines.

29.2.0.en: Ophir: a region in the south of the Arabian Peninsula, distinguished by mines of pure gold, and it is present-day Yemen.

29.2.1.en: Talent: it has several weights ranging between 20 and 40 kg.

29.2.2.en: In addition to what David had prepared for the house of the Lord from the treasuries of the kingdom, he also offered from his own money huge quantities of pure gold and refined silver and gave them to those in charge of the treasuries of the house of the Lord, whom he assigned for this work. This gold was for overlaying the walls of the house of the Lord on the inside. And this shows two things:

29.2.3.en: 1- David's heartfelt love for God, so he gives of his own money, because he has nothing dearer than God.

29.2.4.en: 2- David's generosity in giving, so he gives abundantly the best he has to God.

29.2.5.en: Giving to God shows how much you love Him, for it is your opportunity to express your love and your non-attachment to material things, that is, your esteem of God above everything in the world. And know that giving to any person in need, or to the Church, is very precious in the sight of God, indeed it is your way to enter the Kingdom.

29.3.1.en: To consecrate his service (to fill his hand) to the Lord: gives to God generously.

29.3.2.en: Rulers of the work: those in charge, or the heads of the various crafts, who take part in the building of the house of God.

29.3.3.en: After David showed his concern to give to the house of God, to be an example to the leaders and the people, when he gave what he had prepared to the heads of the various crafts, and David of course did not intend to boast or be proud, but wanted to encourage everyone to give, he asked the leaders of the people, who among you wishes to donate abundantly to the house of God? David did not wish to bind the people and the leaders to fixed sums, but wanted the donation to result from their love of God, that is, to be completely voluntary.

29.4.0.en: A dram of gold: about 8 grams.

29.4.1.en: The leaders of the people were eager and gave generously to the house of the Lord gold, silver, brass, iron and precious stones, and they gave them to Jehiel, who was in charge of the treasuries of the house of the Lord.

29.5.0.en: When David and the people gave to the house of the Lord, God favored them with joy, since they were counted worthy to share in the building of the house of God, that He might dwell in their midst. And this is a grace that God pours out on everyone who gives to God with all his heart.

29.6.0.en: After David had remained for a period lying on his bed because of his old age, he now strengthened himself and stood before the congregation, to bless them not while he was in his bed but in their presence, and he prayed his prayer, which was a model for his people, and indeed for all of us until now in speaking with God, as he begins it by blessing the Lord God of Israel. Here the humility of God appears, that He is named after His people, so He is called the God of Israel, and David declares that God is blessed in Himself from eternity and to eternity, so He has no need of the praise of men, and this shows David's faith and humility.

29.7.0.en: David continues his praise, and declares that to God belong greatness, power, glory and all that is connected with them, for He is the Creator of the universe, that is, heaven and earth, and He is also above all the gods that men think to be gods, because the works of God surpass all that men ascribe to the pagan gods.

29.8.1.en: David completes his praise, saying that to God belong riches and honor, indeed dominion over all men and creation, and consequently God alone is able to strengthen men and support them. Because of all these attributes of God, David says that He is worthy of praise. And praise is the greatest of prayers, because it is pure love for God, without any request of Him.

29.9.0.en: With great humility David declares his weakness, and that of all his people, and his unworthiness to offer anything to God, namely the gifts offered for the building of His Temple, because God is the Creator of everything, so what man offers to God is His own, as if man takes from the hand of God and then gives it back into His hand, so giving is a grace from God to man, so that he may feel that he is offering something to God, because the Owner of everything in the world is God alone.

29.10.0.en: David shows his love for God in his description of himself and of all who believe in God as strangers and sojourners in this world, and consequently not attached to material things, so that they give them easily and with joy to God, since their only aim is the eternal Kingdom. David feels that all the fathers from the days of Abraham lived as strangers, so he is a stranger like them, even if he is a king and has much gold and possessions and greatness, because the love of God has taken possession of his heart and covered over everything, and all that he prepared and offered for the Temple of God is originally God's own.

29.11.0.en: David shows his faith in God, for He is the searcher of hearts and reins and rejoices in the love of His children for Him, and therefore David and his people came forward to give gifts to the house of God, that they might rejoice in this blessing, to offer to God and for God to rejoice in them. Here David's heartfelt love for God appears, for he offers his heart before his material gifts.

29.12.0.en: David intercedes through the fathers whom God blessed before, and entreats His mercies, that the feelings of love for God may remain in the hearts of His people, and that God may establish them in them and prepare their hearts every day to be attached to His love, and this by keeping His commandments. And God's dwelling in the hearts of His people is more important than His dwelling in a house made with hands.

29.13.0.en: Here David makes a special petition for his son Solomon, that his whole heart may be for God, so that he may be concerned for the building of the house of God, whose materials David had prepared, and keep the commandments of God and live by them. And this shows the importance of the leader, for if he is spiritual he will lead his people in life with God.

29.13.1.en: Be concerned for your spiritual life, because you are an example to those around you and you influence them without speaking, so keep the commandments of God and be concerned for His service with all your heart, even if you do not see the completion of what you are doing, or receive any praise, as David prepared the materials for building the Temple though he knew that he would not build it.

29.14.0.en: David appears as a great spiritual leader in calling his people to bless God as he did, so they obeyed him and blessed the Lord and bowed down before Him and before the king, and this was a declaration from them of their support for every word David had said in his prayer, that is, David was the tongue that spoke for the hearts of all his people.

29.15.s.en: (3) The offering of sacrifices and the enthroning of Solomon

29.15.0.en: On the day after David's prayer and his giving of blessing to God, and the people after him, the people gathered and offered peace offerings to God in abundance, rejoicing at Solomon's being made king. The numbers of these sacrifices were a thousand bullocks, and likewise rams, and also lambs. And they ate of the sacrifices before God and made Solomon king the second time, and with him was Zadok the high priest, who remained with him, because Abiathar, the other high priest, had taken part in the conspiracy of Adonijah, and so was removed, that is, Zadok became the only high priest for all the people, and therefore it says "and Zadok to be priest," and this was mentioned in (1 Kgs 2:35). The first enthroning of Solomon was when Zadok the high priest poured the oil on Solomon's head and he entered Jerusalem with a great procession (1 Kgs 1:39, 40). Solomon here is like David, who was anointed by the hand of Samuel while he was in his father's house, but reigned many years later, after Saul died.

29.15.1.en: David and Solomon are types of Christ, who first reigned over the hearts of those who believe in Him by His Incarnation and His redemption of them and the descent of His Holy Spirit upon them, and will then reign completely a second time on the last day, at His Second Coming, when He casts Satan into eternal torment and glorifies those who believe in Him with Him in the Kingdom.

29.16.0.en: Thus Solomon was proclaimed king over the people of God in the lifetime of David, and all the chiefs and mighty men submitted to him, since God gave him grace and awe in their eyes, despite his young age. All his brothers also submitted to him. And the divine majesty that God gave to Solomon surpassed any majesty given to another king over Israel.

29.16.1.en: God is ready to give you awe in the eyes of those around you, however great your weakness, if you trust in Him and are humble, and He will work through you with all power, for the glory of His holy name.

29.17.0.en: This event was mentioned in (1 Kgs 2:11, 12). After David made his son Solomon king, having completed forty years on the throne, seven of them over the tribe of Judah in Hebron and thirty-three years over all Israel in Jerusalem, when his age at that time was seventy years (2 Sam 5:4, 5), David died in a good old age, because his life was good and pleased God, so that God ascribed the kings who came from his descendants to him, and even Christ Himself was ascribed to David, in magnification of David's righteousness and his love for God.

29.17.1.en: God regards every good work you do very highly, and in the end, when you leave this world, you will have a great place in heaven, according to your goodness.

29.18.0.en: What was written here about David, and also what was written in the books of Samuel and the beginning of the First Book of Kings, was recorded, in addition to other accounts, in special historical books that are not among the books of the Bible, namely the acts of Samuel the prophet, the acts of Nathan the prophet and the acts of Gad the seer.
